Isaiah 29 · Woe to Ariel and the Sealed Book

precepts.text: When the Most High turns again the captivity of Zion, they were like them that dream; the nations' desire to destroy Israel will not be fulfilled.
precepts.point: The multitude of nations that fight against Ariel shall be as a dream of a night vision: like a hungry man who dreams he eats but awakes empty, or a thirsty man who dreams he drinks but awakes faint. The nations dream of destroying Israel, but it shall not come to pass, though it will still be like a nightmare to His people.

note.label: Isaiah 29: Woe to Ariel and the Sealed Book

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel” shall be “as a dream of a night vision”, like a hungry man who dreams he eats but “he awaketh, and his soul is empty”, or a thirsty man who dreams he drinks but “he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint”. David speaks of the same dream from the other side: “When the Lord turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream.”

The nations dream of destroying Israel, but it shall not come to pass; their desire will not be fulfilled, and they will wake up empty. And when the Most High turns again the captivity of Zion, his people will be like them that dream too. It will still be like a nightmare to his people, for Israel is contending against the Most High as well as the nations he brings, visited “with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.” But the end of the dream is the nations empty and Zion’s captivity turned.

points: When the Most High turned again the captivity of Zion, we were like them that dream. Then was our mouth filled with laughter and our tongue with singing. Then said they among the heathen, the Most High hath done great things for them.

note.label: Psalm 126: They That Sow in Tears Shall Reap in Joy

points: The Most High hath done great things for us, whereof we are glad. Turn again our captivity, O Lord, as the streams in the south.

note.label: Psalm 126: They That Sow in Tears Shall Reap in Joy

points: This is all going into Israel being saved from the hand of their enemies. Pay attention, all through the psalms it was Israel, Israel, Israel, us, our, we, us. All of these are possessive words used to describe us in our condition. We are sowing in tears right now, but we shall reap in joy.

note.label: Psalm 126: They That Sow in Tears Shall Reap in Joy

points: They that sow in tears shall reap in joy. He that goeth forth and weepeth, bearing precious seed, shall doubtless come again with rejoicing, bringing his sheaves with him.
